**Given:** The finite input, budget $N$, tolerance $\tau$, and operationwise
finite-arithmetic model stated in the algorithm.

[F1] [[alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-deflation-and-residual]] has finite
loops, a finite sweep budget, explicit range-failure handling, and records each
arithmetic residual and each assigned structural zero.

[F2] [[prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-reduction-preserves-form-and-equivalence]]:
the exact initialization gives the finite index schedule and support induction; numerical reconstruction instead uses [F5].

[F3] [[thm-householder-reflectors-and-givens-transformations-are-unitary-and-annihilate-targeted-entries]]:
left and right Givens factors can annihilate the prescribed bulge entries.

[F4] [[lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors-accumulate-for-pencil]]:
local left/right unitary updates with local arithmetic and deflation residuals
give a global perturbation pair bounded by the sum of their pair norms.

[F5] [[lem-qz-two-sided-local-computed-update-bound]] supplies common computed
left/right factors for both matrices, correct row-target orientation, exact
target writes, pulled-back perturbations, and explicit local norm bounds.



1.1 The initialization uses finitely many Givens loops by [F2]. In a QZ sweep, the first left rotation is chosen from the computed first two components of $(\beta H-\alpha T)e_1$, whose only possibly nonzero entries are the first two. The following right rotation removes the new $T_{2,1}$ entry and can create only the bulge $H_{3,1}$. [F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

1.2 For an infinite-deflation step with $T_{k,k}=0$, the descending right rotations make $T_{j,j}=0$ for $j=k-1,\ldots,a$. At each such stage, $T_{j+1,j}=T_{j+1,j+1}=0$, so the right rotation does not create a subdiagonal entry in $T$. It can create only $H_{j+2,j}$, which the paired left rotation zeros; that left rotation preserves triangularity because the affected entries of column $j+1$ of $T$ are both zero. The final left rotation zeros $H_{a+1,a}$ while column $a$ of $T$ remains zero, isolating the top one-by-one pair $(H_{a,a},0)$. The mandatory post-isolation scan reports the $(0,0)$ branch as `singular-pencil-suspected`, so it is not assigned an eigenvalue. The targeted zeros are explicit assignments; applying rounded rotations to other already-zero coordinate pairs preserves them exactly. [F1, F3, F5, induction]

1.3 There are finitely many initialization loops, at most $2n$ rotations per infinite isolation or per active-block sweep, at most $n$ successful infinite removals, and at most $N$ sweeps over at most $n$ active blocks. An unsuccessful isolation exits rather than repeating indefinitely. Each residual/controller evaluation uses finite prescribed factor/column loops. Every scalar operation either succeeds or exits with `range-failure`; missing unitarity or arithmetic certificates exit with `certificate-inconclusive`. Thus every branch terminates with a declared status. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 If the current bulge is $H_{j+1,j-1}$, [F3] supplies a left Givens factor on rows $j,j+1$ that zeros it. This can create the single $T_{j+1,j}$ entry; a right Givens factor on columns $j,j+1$ zeros that entry and can create only the next Hessenberg bulge $H_{j+2,j}$. The final rotation pair has no row below the active block, so the sweep ends Hessenberg-triangular. Computed target entries are explicitly zeroed with [F5], so this support induction also holds in rounded storage. Structural writes are included in their arithmetic allowance; only separate tolerance writes enter the deflation ledger. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, induction]

2.2 For a run with certified factors, each local update has the form $A_j=Q_j^*(A_{j-1}+E_j^A+D_j^A)Z_j$ and $B_j=Q_j^*(B_{j-1}+E_j^B+D_j^B)Z_j$, where $E_j$ includes the structural target write and $D_j$ is the saved separate tolerance write, pulled back from post-action coordinates as required by [F5]. Applying [F4] to this finite list gives $S=Q^*(A+\Delta_A)Z$ and $T=Q^*(B+\Delta_B)Z$ for the accumulated pair $(\Delta_A,\Delta_B)$. No bound is asserted without local norm certificates. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Before `qz-computed`, both arrays are triangular and all diagonal pairs are nonzero. Their homogeneous determinant is $\prod_k(\beta S_{kk}-\alpha T_{kk})$, a product of nonzero linear polynomials, hence is not identically zero. The returned pencil is regular; any label with second coordinate zero is an infinite candidate of this returned perturbed pencil. This proves no exact original-input infinite-eigenvalue or forward-error claim. [F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** Successful source arithmetic, including normal nonzero exact intermediates and admissible stored basis constants $0,1$ for residual evaluation. All controller arithmetic is exact, separate from rounded matrix/vector updates.

[F1] [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] fixes the stored Givens generator, two-product/one-addition application, exact conjugations and target writes.

[F2] [[lem-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-local-backward-error]] proves the unitary representative, raw application coefficient $q+\sqrt2(7u+6u^2)(1+q)$ and target-write bound $u+2q$ plus that raw coefficient.

[F3] [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]] bounds successful sequential stored-input matrix-vector products by $g_n\|A\|_F\|x\|_2$, and final componentwise subtraction by $u(\|y\|_2+\|s\|_2)$.



1.1 Replacing $\sqrt2$ by $2$ enlarges the source's raw coefficient to $v$ and its raw intended-zero bound to $h$. Apply the raw bound separately to $C,D$, square and add: the common action's pair discrepancy is at most $vP(C,D)$. The one actual target write has norm at most $h$ times its two-entry target norm, hence at most $hP(C,D)$. The triangle inequality gives $\eta P(C,D)$. This uses one generated factor for both arrays; no similarity relation between $C,D$ is assumed. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Permutations and conjugate transposes preserve Euclidean/Frobenius norms and use exact copies of stored coefficients. Write $U(rJ)^*=(\rho,\epsilon)^T$ for the normalized rounded representative, without assuming $\epsilon=0$. Conjugate transposition and multiplication by $J$ give $rJU^*J=(\overline\epsilon,\overline\rho)$. The source intended-zero allowance bounds $|\epsilon|$ by $(u+2q)\|r\|_2$; the rounded right application contributes at most $v\|r\|_2$, so its first-coordinate overwrite has the inherited bound $h\|r\|_2$ of step 1.1. For a second-coordinate right target write $Ur^*=(\rho,\epsilon)^T$, giving $rU^*=(\overline\rho,\overline\epsilon)$ and the same bound on that target. Thus the stated orientations select the correct coordinate without asserting exact annihilation by the normalized rounded representative. An external vector chooses a unitary but does not license any matrix zero assignment. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Write the computed pair as $Q_0^*(C,D)Z_0+F$ in post-action coordinates. Define $E=Q_0FZ_0^*$ componentwise. Unitarity gives the stated update and preserves the pair norm. Pull a separately recorded post-action write back in the same way; its saved entry and factors specify it exactly. For two consecutive actions the intermediate pair norm is at most $(1+\ell_L)P(C,D)$, so the sum of their pulled-back errors is at most $[\ell_L+\ell_R(1+\ell_L)]P(C,D)$. Pure deflation uses identity factors. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra, construct]

3.2 If $y$ differs from the exact current vector by at most $e$, the next raw action differs from the corresponding exact unitary action on $y$ by at most $v\|y\|_2$. That exact unitary preserves the preceding discrepancy, proving the recurrence. Rightmost factors act first in a matrix product, which gives the specified orders for $Ze_k$ and $Q^*$ action. Adjoints and reversals inherit the raw bound from step 2.1. [given, F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Apply [F3] to the STORED vector $\widehat z$, then transport $\widehat z-Ze_k$ through $A$ using $\|A\|_2\le\|A\|_F$. Step 3.2 propagates this discrepancy through $Q^*$. The final subtraction allowance in [F3] gives $e_k$. Each exact residual column is therefore bounded by $\|\widehat r_k\|_2+e_k$; the square root of the sum of their squares is at most their sum. This proves the residual certificate without using nonstored normalized factor entries as floating inputs. [F3, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 For any finite complex array, its Frobenius/Euclidean norm is at most the sum of absolute real and imaginary components, by squaring and the nonnegative cross terms. These sums and the rational constants $v,h,\eta,g_n$ use only finite field operations, absolute-value comparisons and the prescribed finite loops. Every denominator is positive under the stated hypotheses. Exact rational arithmetic realizes these instructions for rational stored data; no bit-cost bound is asserted. If an excluded rounded operation or dimension hypothesis fails, that evaluation produces no certificate, as specified. [given, step 1.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The stated real/complex arithmetic realization and successful no-underflow operations.

[F1] [[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]] fixes the scaled norm, coefficient formation, product order, zero branches and exact target writes.

[F2] [[lem-product-of-one-plus-deltas-gives-theta-n]] bounds products of rounding factors and sequential addition expansions.



1.1 A complex product's real/imaginary error is at most $2(2u+u^2)|z||w|\le6u|z||w|$: bound each of its four real products and then its two component additions. A sequential complex dot of length $r$ therefore has error at most $[6u+\gamma_{r-1}(1+6u)]\sum_i|z_i||w_i|=g\sum_i|z_i||w_i|$. These expansions include exact zeros. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 A scaled norm with $2r$ real components has its positive squared sum multiplied termwise by between $(1-u)^{2r+2}$ and $(1+u)^{2r+2}$, including two scaling factors. Square root and rescaling give relative norm error at most $e$. The independently scaled modulus of $x_1$ has lower/upper factors $(1-u)^4,(1+u)^4$, so the phase division error relative to $x_1/|x_1|$ is at most $a_\phi$; when $x_1=0$ it is zero. Thus for $N=\|x\|$, $\alpha_0=-\operatorname{phase}(x_1)N$ and $v_0=x-\alpha_0e_1$, one has $|\widehat\alpha-\alpha_0|\le a_\alpha N$ and $\|v-v_0\|\le d_vN$. For exponents at least one the lower deviation is bounded by the upper by convexity, justifying these two-sided estimates. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The identity $H(v)^*H(v)=I$ follows by multiplying $I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$. The exact phase choice gives $H(v_0)x=\alpha_0e_1$ and $\|v_0\|\ge N$ by direct inner-product expansion. Normalization gives $\|a/\|a\|-b/\|b\|\|\le2\|a-b\|/\|b\|$; expanding the difference of unit-vector projectors therefore gives $\|H(v)-H(v_0)\|\le8d_v$. The target-column error is at most $(a_\alpha+8d_v)N$. [step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 For Givens formation at stored $z,w$, the norm $h$ has relative factors between $(1-u)^3$ and $(1+u)^3$, since its unscaled four-component squared sum has at most four rounding factors per term. The norm $n_z$ has exponents two. Let $G_0$ be the exact canonical Givens annihilator for $(z,w)$, with coefficients $c_0=|z|/\|(z,w)\|$ and $s_0=(z/|z|)\overline w/\|(z,w)\|$ when $z\ne0$. The phase error is at most $a_2$; the coefficient numerator, denominator, six-operation complex product and division errors therefore give $|c-c_0|\le q c_0$ and $|s-s_0|\le q|s_0|$. If $z=0$, $c=0$ and $s_0=\overline w/|w|$; the smaller bound $(1+u)/(1-u)^3-1\le q$ applies. Hence $\|(c,s)-(c_0,s_0)\|\le q$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The positive real sum defining $w$ has bounds $(1-u)^{2r}\|v\|^2\le w\le(1+u)^{2r}\|v\|^2$. The final division gives $|\widehat\tau\|v\|^2/2-1|\le a_\tau$. The dot-product error in step 1.1, the componentwise real multiplication by $\widehat\tau$ and the final complex multiplication bound the rank-one update error by $c_U\|B\|_F$. Final subtraction adds at most $u(3+c_U)\|B\|_F$. Combine this with step 2.1 over disjoint columns to get the Householder bound. For the zero column take the identity exactly. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Put $t=\sqrt{c^2+|s|^2}>0$ and $Q=T/t$. Direct multiplication gives $T^*T=t^2I$, so $Q$ is canonical unitary, $\|T-Q\|=|t-1|\le q$ and $\|T\|\le1+q$. Normalization also gives $\|Q-G_0\|\le2q$; differences of canonical blocks have norm equal to the Euclidean norm of their coefficient differences. Each computed output entry has error at most $(7u+6u^2)(|c||C_{1j}|+|s||C_{2j}|)$, by two products and their addition. The absolute coefficient block has norm at most $\sqrt2t$. Thus the raw update differs from $QC$ by at most $v\|C\|_F$. [step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Scaling introduced $\|\lambda(z,w)-(a,b)\|\le u\|(a,b)\|$. Because $G_0$ annihilates $(z,w)$, its exact target residual for $(a,b)$ is at most $u\|(a,b)\|$; under $Q$ it is at most $(u+2q)\|(a,b)\|$. Writing the rounded target to zero adds at most $(u+2q+v)\|(a,b)\|$ to the raw update discrepancy, so the total is at most $\eta_G\|C\|_F$. No unrelated matrix entry is zeroed for a shift-vector rotation. Identity branches have zero discrepancy. [F1, step 2.2, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 In every left case choose $E=W^*C_+-C$, with $W=H(v)$ or $Q$; unitarity gives the stated equation and equal error norm. Right updates follow by conjugate transposition and invariance of Frobenius norm. All coefficients are finite explicit functions under the stated conditions, vanish at $u=0$, and have first derivatives bounded by a fixed multiple of the active dimension, proving the asymptotics. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra, construct] ∎

**Given:** The stated stored inputs, evaluation order and successful operations; every nonzero exact intermediate is normal, and zero operations are exact.

[F1] [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] specifies real component operations and six-real-operation complex multiplication.

[F2] [[lem-product-of-one-plus-deltas-gives-theta-n]] bounds sequential addition coefficient errors.



1.1 For $(a+ib)(c+id)$, each rounded real product has error at most $u$ times its absolute exact value. Each final real addition contributes at most $u(1+u)$ times the two corresponding product magnitudes. The Euclidean norm of the resulting real/imaginary error is at most $2(2u+u^2)|a+ib||c+id|\le6u|a+ib||c+id|$, since $u<1$. Conjugation is exact. Real products obey this conservative bound as well. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 In a length-$k$ dot product, each product error from step 1.1 is propagated through at most $k-1$ additions. Expansion of each real component and [F2] bound the dot discrepancy by $[6u+\gamma_{k-1}(1+6u)]\sum_i|a_i||x_i|=g_k\sum_i|a_i||x_i|$, with $\gamma_0=0$. Combining rows and applying Cauchy-Schwarz gives $\|\widehat v-Ax\|_2\le g_nFX=V$. Componentwise subtraction has vector error at most $u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$, so the linear residual allowance is $W$. Zeros cause no difficulty in this expansion. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply step 2.1 to $A^*\widehat w$ to get $\|\widehat z-A^*\widehat w\|_2\le g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2$. Transporting the earlier error through $A^*$ adds at most $FW$. The scalar product error is at most $u\lambda X$; the last addition adds at most $u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2)$. Their sum proves $\rho$. For basis columns, the triangle inequality combines each computed linear residual with its allowance; summing the squared column bounds gives a Frobenius certificate for $I-AB$, which bounds its induced Euclidean norm by Cauchy-Schwarz. [F1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
